description:
NEW MODULE: OctoPi.Coder.Extension.Manager (GenServer)
FILE: apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/extension/manager.ex

Extension.Manager is a GenServer started by the coding agent process via start_link (linked). When the agent dies the Manager and everything under it dies cleanly. When an extension Agent crashes the agent is unaffected.

WHAT EXTENSION.MANAGER DOES IN init/1:
1. Starts a DynamicSupervisor (linked, internal). This supervisor owns extension Agent processes. Agent crashes are absorbed here and do NOT propagate to Extension.Manager.
2. Starts a session-scoped Registry (keys: :duplicate) for custom event pub/sub. Extensions subscribe/publish via this Registry.
3. Calls Loader.load_all/1 with the session extension paths.
4. For each stateful extension: calls DynamicSupervisor.start_child(dynamic_sup, {Agent, fn -> initial_state end}). Extension.Manager is NOT linked to Agents directly -- the DynamicSupervisor owns them.
5. Creates and owns three ETS tables (session-scoped, NOT global atom names):
   - :bag   {event_type, ext_id, handler_fn}  (read_concurrency: true)
   - :set   {tool_name, tool_def}              (read_concurrency: true)
   - :set   {flag_name, flag_value}            (read_concurrency: true)
6. Populates all three tables from the loaded [Extension.t()] list.
No explicit terminate/2 cleanup needed: DynamicSupervisor is linked and stops with Extension.Manager; ETS tables die when the owning process dies.

HOW AGENTS ARE STARTED (requires coordinating change with opi-fin.2.2):
The macro currently generates Agent.start_link. Change it to use DynamicSupervisor.start_child instead, so the Agent is under the supervisor, not linked to whatever process called init/1.
Mechanism: add agent_supervisor: pid() | nil to API.t(). Extension.Manager sets this field before calling Module.init/1 for each extension (API.put_agent_supervisor(api, dynamic_sup_pid)). The macro reads api.agent_supervisor at runtime and calls DynamicSupervisor.start_child if set, falls back to Agent.start_link if nil (for tests using load_from_factory without a supervisor).
Extension authors never see or set this field.

CRASH ISOLATION:
Agent crash -> DynamicSupervisor absorbs it (supervisors trap exits) -> Extension.Manager unaffected -> coding agent unaffected. Next handler call to that Agent raises -> Dispatcher.safe_call catches it, logs warning, returns nil. Extension degrades silently. Session continues.

PUBLIC API:
  Extension.Manager.start_link(opts) where opts: %{extension_paths: [...]}
  Extension.Manager.table_refs(pid) -> %{handlers: tid, tools: tid, flags: tid}
  Extension.Manager.extensions(pid) -> [Extension.t()]
  Extension.Manager.registry(pid) -> pid

DISPATCHER CHANGE:
Add handlers_table: :ets.tid() to Context.t(). Coding agent sets it from Extension.Manager.table_refs/1 when building Context before each dispatch. Dispatcher.all_handlers/2 reads from the table instead of scanning [Extension.t()].

TEST: extension/manager_test.exs
- Two Manager instances with same paths have independent Agents and independent ETS tables (session isolation)
- An Agent killed with Process.exit does not crash Extension.Manager
- Dispatcher.emit reads correct handlers from table
title: ETS handler dispatch table
